title: What the less common app profile settings do

prose.text: Most settings in `policyExtension` have their own description in the API document. These are the ones whose effect is worth knowing before changing them.

prose.label: Traffic handling.
prose.text: {{tunnel-internal-traffic}} Its default on Windows is open {{gap:tunnel-internal-default}}. {{intercept-all-adapters}} {{v8-pac}}

prose.label: Reauthentication.
prose.text: {{reauth-period-hours}} The API document says seconds instead: [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:reauth-period-unit]]. {{zpa-auth-expiry}}

prose.label: On-Net policy.
prose.text: {{on-net-policy-sdk}} It is the profile's forwarding profile, embedded: [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:onnetpolicy-embedded]].

prose.label: Android cellular settings.
prose.text: {{android-quota}} {{android-mms}} {{android-key-candidates}} What `enforced` does, and whether those name matches hold, is open {{gap:android-field-roles}}.

drop-quic.statement: On the iOS and Android profiles, Drop QUIC Traffic exists because Z-Tunnel 1.0 does not support QUIC (UDP 443): when enabled, Z-Tunnel 1.0 drops QUIC packets so the application can fall back to TCP 443. The API document describes `policyExtension.dropQuicTraffic` the same way.
drop-quic.conditions: Scoped to iOS and Android (coordinator follow-up to the w2 verify): the help article lists the option only in the iOS and Android sections, not in the Windows, macOS or Linux sections.

evidence.after: The Add iOS Policy window appears.
quotes: Drop QUIC Traffic: This option is for websites that use QUIC (UDP 443), which is not supported by Z-Tunnel 1.0. When enabled, Z-Tunnel 1.0 drops QUIC packets so the application can fall back to TCP 443.

evidence.after: The Add Android Policy window appears.
quotes: Drop QUIC Traffic: This option is for websites that use QUIC (UDP 443), which is not supported by Z-Tunnel 1.0. When enabled, Z-Tunnel 1.0 drops QUIC packets so the application can fall back to TCP 443.

expect.description: Indicates if drop QUIC traffic is enabled. When enabled, Z-Tunnel 1.0 drops QUIC packets so the application can fall back to TCP 443.

truncate-dns.statement: Truncate ZPA Large UDP DNS Response truncates DNS responses over 512 bytes so the query is retried over TCP.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Truncate ZPA Large UDP DNS Response: Enable to truncate DNS responses that exceed 512 bytes to retry the DNS query over TCP.

expect.description: Indicates whether Truncate Large UDP DNS response is enabled to truncate DNS responses that exceed 512 bytes to retry the DNS query over TCP.

clear-kerberos-dc.statement: Clear Kerberos DC (`purgeKerberosPreferredDCCache`) clears the cached list of Kerberos preferred domain controllers when the app connects to and disconnects from Private Access; Windows 4.5 and later only.

quotes: Clear Kerberos DC: Enable to clear the list of Kerberos preferred domain controllers in the cache when Zscaler Client Connector connects to and disconnects from Private Access.

expect.description: Indicates whether purge Kerberos Preferred DC Cache is enabled. When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector clears the list of Kerberos-preferred domain controllers in the cache when connected to and disconnected from ZPA. Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5 and later for Windows.

anti-tampering.statement: Anti-tampering prevents users from stopping or modifying Zscaler endpoint products; a timer of 0 to 1440 minutes re-enables the app after a user disables it with a one-time password, and on Windows 4.5 and later the profile setting can override the install-time anti-tampering option.

quotes: Anti-tampering protection prevents end users from stopping and modifying Zscaler endpoint products.

You can set a timer to re-enable Zscaler Client Connector if a user disables it using the one-time password (OTP). In the Reactivate Anti-Tampering After (In Mins) field, enter a value between 0 and 1440 minutes.

Override Anti Tampering Install Parameter: Enable to use the Enable Anti-tampering setting from the app profile regardless of how the --enableAntiTampering or ENABLEANTITAMPERING install option was set during installation. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5 and later for Windows only.

anti-tampering.conditions: Quote extended to cover "Windows 4.5 and later" (verifier w2 A11).

reactivate-zia.statement: Reactivate ZIA After turns Internet & SaaS back on 1 to 1440 minutes after a user turns it off; 0 disables reactivation.

evidence.after: Win V4.7 and Older Client Configuration:
quotes: To enable the reactivation period, enter any value from 1 to 1440 minutes. To disable, enter 0 (zero) so that Zscaler Client Connector doesn't reactivate Internet & SaaS after the user turns it off.

send-disable-reason.statement: Send Disable Service Reason, off by default, lets users describe why they disabled a service; the reason shows in device details, and the API exports disable reasons as a CSV report.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Send Disable Service Reason: This option allows users to send a description about why a Zscaler service (e.g., Internet & SaaS, Private Access, ZDX) was disabled on a device. By default, this option is disabled. This information is accessible when viewing device details.

expect.description: Downloads or exports a report as a CSV file showing the disable reasons of a device.

fail-close-lockdown.statement: A fail-close option makes the app fail close while a tunnel is starting or restarting, for example after login, Repair App or Restart Service.

expect.description: Option to have Zscaler Client Connector fail close while a tunnel is starting or restarting (e.g., after a user logs in to the device or out of the app, clicks Repair App or clicks Restart Service).

lockdown-on-errors.statement: Two more fail-close options apply to Windows 4.7 and later: Lockdown on Firewall Error fails close while a firewall or antivirus program blocks the app's traffic (an End FW/AV Error), and Lockdown on Driver Error fails close while a Windows Lightweight Filter (LWF) driver error keeps the app from starting a tunnel.

quotes: Lockdown on Firewall Error: Enable this option to have Zscaler Client Connector fail close while a firewall or antivirus program is blocking Zscaler Client Connector traffic (i.e., an End FW/AV Error). Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later for Windows.

Lockdown on Driver Error: Enable this option to have Zscaler Client Connector fail close while a Windows Lightweight Filter (LWF) driver error is preventing Zscaler Client Connector from starting a tunnel. Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later for Windows.

lockdown-error-keys.statement: By name, these two options are `policyExtension.zccFailCloseSettingsLockdownOnFirewallError` and `zccFailCloseSettingsLockdownOnDriverError`, which the Go SDK carries and the API document's edit body does not.
lockdown-error-keys.conditions: The key-to-option mapping is by name; no source states it. The absence from the API document's edit-body policyExtension is pinned.

quotes: `json:"zccFailCloseSettingsLockdownOnFirewallError,omitempty"`
`json:"zccFailCloseSettingsLockdownOnDriverError,omitempty"`

highlight-active-control.statement: Highlight Active Control (`highlightActiveControl`) displays an outline around an actively selected control in the app; Windows 2.1.2 and later.

quotes: Highlight Active Control: Enable this option to display an outline around an actively selected control. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 2.1.2 and later for Windows.

expect.description: Indicates whether an outline around an actively selected control is displayed.

dns-settings.statement: The API document describes four DNS keys in `policyExtension`: `useDefaultAdapterForDNS` binds the trusted-hostname DNS lookup to the adapter whose trust is being evaluated, `disableDNSRouteExclusion` concerns excluding DNS servers from the routing table, `prioritizeDnsExclusions` puts Domain Exclusions ahead of Domain Inclusions, and `enforceSplitDNS` makes the app handle DNS traffic for the desired (ZPA) domains only.
dns-settings.conditions: Added from the API document's descriptions (verifier w2 A15); the legacy rows for these keys had been dropped as generated, but the generated layer carries no descriptions for policyExtension.

expect.description: Indicates whether Default Adapter for DNS is enabled. When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector force binds the Trusted Hostname IP resolution DNS request to the Adapter whose trust is being evaluated.
Indicates if DNS server route exclusion is disabled. When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector excludes DNS servers from the routing table.
Indicates whether Prioritize DNS Exclusions is enabled. When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector prioritizes DNS domains in Domain Exclusions over Domain Inclusions.
Indicates whether Enforce Split DNS is enabled. When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector is enforced to handle DNS traffic of desired (ZPA) domains only.

zpa-auth-expiry.statement: Force ZPA authentication to expire can trigger Private Access expiry on system sleep or hibernation, system restart, a network IP change, a Windows logon session start (Windows 4.5 and later) and a Windows session lock held for 1 to 60 minutes (Windows 4.6 and later). The API document carries these as `policyExtension.zpaAuthExp*` keys; it describes `zpaAuthExpSessionLockStateMinTimeInSecond` in minutes although the key name says seconds.
zpa-auth-expiry.conditions: Added from the help and the API document's descriptions (verifier w2 A15). The key-to-option mapping follows the matching descriptions.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: On System Sleep/Hibernate: Trigger expiration when the system is put into sleep or hibernation mode.
On System Restart: Trigger expiration when the system is restarted.
On Network IP Change: Trigger expiration if the network IP changes.
Windows Logon Session Start: Trigger expiration when a user logs in, even if fast startup is enabled. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5 and later for Windows.

Windows Session Lock: Trigger expiration after a Windows user has been locked for the number of minutes in the Minimum Time in Locked State (In Minutes). You can enter a number of minutes from 1 to 60. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.6 and later for Windows.

expect.description: ZPA authentication to expire on System Sleep/Hibernate.
ZPA authentication to expire on system restart.
ZPA authentication to expire on Network IP Change.
ZPA authentication expires when the Windows session has locked.
Trigger expiration after a Windows user has been locked for the duration specified in the Minimum Time in Locked State (in minutes).

tunnel-internal-traffic.statement: Tunnel Internal Client Connector Traffic (`tunnelZappTraffic`) sends the app's own traffic, such as app and policy updates, through Zscaler; it applies only in no-default-route deployments (Windows 2.12 and later), PAC requests still go direct, and when disabled internal traffic goes direct. The Go SDK's UI-captured macOS and iOS defaults set it to 0.
tunnel-internal-traffic.conditions: Key name and capture defaults added (verifier w2 A4): the API document's description of tunnelZappTraffic matches the help text; the Go defaults are UI captures for macOS and iOS only.

expect.description: Indicates whether Tunnel Zapp Traffic is enabled. When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector tunnels internal traffic through Zscaler, and continues to send PAC requests directly.

quotes: TunnelZappTraffic:            0,
TunnelZappTraffic:         0,

evidence.after: Win V4.7 and Older Client Configuration:
quotes: Tunnel Internal Client Connector Traffic: Enable this option for Zscaler Client Connector to tunnel internal traffic (e.g., app updates and policy updates) through Zscaler.

This option is only applicable if you deploy in a no-default route environment and applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 2.12 and later for Windows. If disabled, Zscaler Client Connector sends internal traffic directly.
When this option is enabled, Zscaler Client Connector does not tunnel PAC requests and continues to send PAC requests directly.

intercept-all-adapters.statement: Intercept ZIA traffic makes the app intercept Internet & SaaS traffic from all network adapters; it applies only to Tunnel mode with the Packet Filter Based driver.

quotes: Intercept ZIA traffic: Enable this option to have Zscaler Client Connector intercept Internet & SaaS traffic from all network adapters. This setting only applies to Tunnel Mode with a Packet Filter Based driver.

v8-pac.statement: The V8 JavaScript based PAC parser option compiles PAC JavaScript with Google's V8 engine; Windows 4.9 and later use it regardless of the setting.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: V8 JavaScript based PAC Parser: Enable Google's open-source V8 engine to compile JavaScript for the PAC parser.
Zscaler Client Connector version 4.9 and later for Windows uses the V8 JavaScript based PAC parser regardless of this setting.

reauth-period-hours.statement: The Python SDK documents `reauth_period` as the re-authentication period in hours.

quotes: reauth_period (str): Re-authentication period (in hours).

location-rulesets.statement: With Location Policy Override (Windows 4.8 and later, with the WFP driver installed), a profile assigns a location ruleset per network type: On-Trusted and Off-Trusted are required, VPN-Trusted and Split VPN-Trusted default to the On-Trusted ruleset. The Go SDK always sends both VPN entries, with id 0 when none is bound.

quotes: This feature is available only for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for Windows, and you must first enable Install WFP Driver.

You must select a ruleset for On-Trusted Network and for Off-Trusted Network. For VPN-Trusted Network and Split VPN-Trusted Network, the default value is Same as "On-Trusted Network," but you can change or clear it.
Both nested entries are present even when no ruleset is bound (their

end-to-end-diagnostics.statement: The Go SDK models `endToEndDiagnostics` as a toggle per network context (trusted, VPN-trusted, off-trusted, split-VPN-trusted) that the macOS web policy carries at the top level and also embeds as JSON in `policyExtension.zdxLiteConfigObj`.

quotes: EndToEndDiagnostics is the per-network-context end-to-end diagnostics
toggle the macOS web policy ships at the top level (and embedded as
JSON inside policyExtension.zdxLiteConfigObj).

on-net-policy-sdk.statement: `onNetPolicy` is not a separate On-Net policy: the API document describes it as the policies that define how the app treats traffic in the ZIA and ZPA services, with the forwarding profile's properties. The application-profile PATCH body carries it and the web policy edit body does not; Python's web policy model reads its trusted-network fields (`conditionType`, `predefinedTrustedNetworks`, `predefinedTnAll`) and Go's application-profile model carries it untyped, while Go's web policy struct has no such key.
on-net-policy-sdk.conditions: Restated (verifier w2 A2): the earlier wording left it as a separate On-Net setting. That it is the forwarding profile rests on the description and property set in the API document; the edit-body absence is pinned, and the Go WebPolicy struct was searched for onNetPolicy.

expect.description: Specifies the policies to define how Zscaler Client Connector treats traffic from user systems in the ZIA and ZPA services.
Specifies the policies to define how Zscaler Client Connector treats traffic from user systems in the ZIA and ZPA services.

quotes: self.predefined_tn_all = config["predefinedTnAll"] if "predefinedTnAll" in config else None
OnNetPolicy interface{} `json:"onNetPolicy,omitempty"`

zdp-service.statement: `enableZdpService` turns on the Zscaler Data Protection (ZDP) service, which installs the ZDP endpoint.

expect.description: Indicates whether Zscaler Data Protection (ZDP) service is enabled to install ZDP endpoint.

android-quota.statement: Android profiles carry cellular data quota settings: a quota, optionally enforced only while roaming, reset on a chosen monthly billing day, and a Wi-Fi SSID for testing and simulating data usage. Zscaler has ended support of bandwidth quota control for Client Connector 1.5.3 and later for Android.
android-quota.conditions: Qualified with the end of support for quota control (verifier w2 A5).

quotes: Zscaler ended support of bandwidth quota control for Zscaler Client Connector version 1.5.3 and later for Android.
Enforce Quota Only for Roaming Users: Enable to enforce the quota only when users are roaming.
The day you select is when the cellular quota is reset every month
Wi-Fi SSID: (Optional) Enter the service set identifier (SSID) of your wireless local area network (WLAN) if you want to test and simulate data usage for that specific SSID.

android-mms.statement: Bypass Traffic for MMS Applications makes the app bypass standard Android messaging apps, including Android Messages.

quotes: Bypass Traffic for MMS Applications: Enable this option for Zscaler Client Connector to automatically bypass standard messaging applications on Android.

android-key-candidates.statement: By name, three keys in the API document's `androidPolicy` block match help settings: `allowedApps` the Android Applications on Allowlist (app identifiers excluded from the quota calculation), `bypassAndroidApps` Bypass Traffic for Specific Application (an app identifier to bypass), and `customText` the Block Notification Message shown when the quota is exceeded.
android-key-candidates.conditions: Name-match candidates only (verifier w2 A6); no source maps these keys to the settings.

quotes: Android Applications on Allowlist: (Optional) To allowlist Android applications:
Add the apps' identifiers, separated by commas, to exclude apps from the quota calculation.
Bypass Traffic for Specific Application: Enter the identifier of any Android application to configure a bypass for it.
Block Notification Message: (Optional) Enter or paste text of the notification that appears when the quota is exceeded.

tunnel-internal-default.title: Default of Tunnel Internal Client Connector Traffic on Windows
tunnel-internal-default.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "tunnel_zapp_traffic default / typical value — the field exists in both SDKs but neither encodes a default." The key is now sourced (the API document describes `tunnelZappTraffic` with the help's wording), and the Go SDK's UI-captured macOS and iOS defaults are 0: see tunnel-internal-traffic. The setting applies to Windows, and no Windows capture or source gives its default there.

android-field-roles.title: What enforced does, and whether allowedApps, bypassAndroidApps and customText are the settings their names suggest
android-field-roles.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "allowed_apps — allowlist of apps that ZCC manages on Android; bypass_android_apps — apps that bypass ZCC on Android; enforced — whether ZCC is enforced (cannot be disabled) on Android; custom_text — custom notification text shown to Android users." The help's allowlist excludes apps from the quota calculation, which contradicts "apps that ZCC manages" if allowedApps is that allowlist; the name-match candidates are in android-key-candidates. No source describes `enforced`.

unverified-field-roles.title: What enableFlowBasedTunnel does
unverified-field-roles.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "enableFlowBasedTunnel — flow-based tunnel mode (alternative to packet-based)". Both SDKs carry the key; the API document and the help do not describe it. Two other legacy roles are settled: "highlightActiveControl — UI polish, highlight the active rule in ZCC's local admin UI" is contradicted by highlight-active-control (an outline around the selected control), and "zccFailCloseSettingsLockdownOnFirewallError / OnDriverError — fail-close lockdown options when ZCC core fails" is narrowed by lockdown-on-errors and lockdown-error-keys.
